 Judgment
The petitioners in O.P.(M.V.) No.848/2014 on the file of the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-IV, Palakkad, are the appellants herein.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-IV, Palakkad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.

The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the mother and brother of the deceased by name Alex Antony, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08.06.2014.

According to them, on 08.06.2014 at about 05.30 p.m, while the deceased was riding pillion on a motorcycle, another motorcycle bearing Registration No.KL-46-6698 ridden by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit on his motorcycle and as a result of which he fell down and sustained serious injuries and he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver cum owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was limited to Rs.10,00,000/-
4.

The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of MACA NO. 3611 OF 2017 2025:KER:22269 the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A23.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.9.56.000/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri.Baby Mathew, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners/appellants, and Sri.P.Bharathan, the learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.

One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is that deceased was a plus one student aged 17 on the date of the accident, that he was also a bright student engaged several activities including sports, dance and literature and in spite of that, the tribunal has fixed his notional income at Rs.7,000/- which is on the lower side.

2 11.

entities.text: Sheela vs Oriental Insurance Company. Ltd

sentences.text:
The learned counsel has relied upon Exts.A10 to A23 which are MACA NO. 3611 OF 2017 2025:KER:22269 merit certificates received by the deceased for various items like sports, dance,
English recitation, drama, yoga, painting, etc.
He was also a winner of the Bala Ratna in painting in the All India Childrens Competition in the year 2016.

Therefore, it can be seen that the deceased was a very bright student and he was also actively involved in various extra curricular activities including sports, music, painting, literature etc.
12.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, during the year 2014 will come to Rs.9,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the decision in Mekala v. Malathi M and Another [2014 (11) SCC 178], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has fixed the notional income of a XIth standard student at Rs.10,000/- and 50% of the income was added towards future prospects who died in an accident which arose in 2005.

entities.text: Mekala v. Malathi M and Another [2014 (11) SCC 178]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the above circumstance, considering the entire facts, I hold that in the instant case, the notional income of the deceased can be fixed at Rs.12,000/-.
13.
On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 17 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was a bachelor who left behind 2 dependents, towards personal and living expense, 1/2 of the MACA NO. 3611 OF 2017 2025:KER:22269 income is liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).

In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.18,14,400/-.
14.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses and no amount was awarded towards loss of consortium and Rs.1,00,000/- towards love and affection.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, and the dependents (parents, children and spouse) are entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.
Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/- each.

Towards loss of consortium,
petitioners together are entitled to get a sum of Rs.96,800/- (48,400 x 1).

15. Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020)9 SCC 644.

entities.text:
New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020)9 SCC 644
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation awarded towards love and affection is to be deducted.
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the petitioners, is on the lower side.
The deceased died in this case on the date of the accident.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is MACA NO. 3611 OF 2017 2025:KER:22269 on the lower side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 2nd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.19,29,100/- (Rupees Nineteen Lakh MACA NO. 3611 OF 2017 2025:KER:22269 Twenty Nine Thousand One Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till realisation/deposit, excluding interest for a period of 165 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

(enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).
20.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, during the year 2014 will come to Rs.9,500/-.
In the decision in Mekala v. Malathi M and Another [2014 (11) SCC 178], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has fixed the notional income of a XIth standard student at Rs.10,000/- and 50% of the income was added towards future prospects who died in an accident which arose in 2005.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

Somwati and Others, (2020)9 SCC 644.
